## Research question

How much of the price-per-ping gap between high-rise and walk-up apartment
sales in our 2026 Taipei sample remains after accounting for district and
floor area?

This is an associational analysis of recorded transactions. The estimates do
not show that changing a building's type would cause its price to change.

## Team workflow and handoffs

| Role | Responsibility | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Data and sample | Confirm the cleaned file, variable units, eligibility rules, and district-by-building-type counts. | Approve the common analysis sample. |
| 2. Modeling | Fit all three models below on the same rows and check coefficient direction and reference group. | Provide model estimates and intervals. |
| 3. Results and checks | Interpret the comparison, inspect residual patterns, and assess whether district coverage supports an extension. | Provide the main finding and limitations. |
| 4. Report and presentation | Render this report, prepare the results slide, and coordinate final review. | Share the rendered report and presentation. |

## 1. Prepare the analysis sample

The cleaning script produces the processed CSV. This report narrows it to
2026 sales classified as high-rise or walk-up apartments, with positive price
per ping and floor area and a recorded district. The same resulting rows are
used in all three models.
```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(scales)
```

```{r}
required_packages <- c("sandwich", "ggplot2")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install required packages first: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

sales <- read.csv(
  "data/processed/taipei_residential_sales.csv",
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

required_columns <- c(
  "year", "building_group", "price_per_ping_10k_ntd", "FAREA", "DISTRICT"
)
missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(sales))
if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}

analysis_data <- subset(
  sales,
  year == 2026 &
    building_group %in% c("High-rise (11+ floors)", "Walk-up apartment") &
    is.finite(price_per_ping_10k_ntd) & price_per_ping_10k_ntd > 0 &
    is.finite(FAREA) & FAREA > 0 &
    !is.na(DISTRICT) & nzchar(DISTRICT)
)

analysis_data$building_group <- factor(
  analysis_data$building_group,
  levels = c("Walk-up apartment", "High-rise (11+ floors)")
)
analysis_data$DISTRICT <- factor(analysis_data$DISTRICT)
analysis_data$log_price_per_ping <- log(analysis_data$price_per_ping_10k_ntd)
analysis_data$log_area <- log(analysis_data$FAREA)

if (nrow(analysis_data) == 0) {
  stop("No eligible 2026 high-rise or walk-up sales were found.")
}

cat("Analysis sample size:", nrow(analysis_data), "\n")
table(analysis_data$building_group)
with(analysis_data, table(DISTRICT, building_group))
```

**Check before continuing.** Confirm the counts and the district table. The
current snapshot is expected to give 247 eligible transactions, with 158
high-rises and 89 walk-up apartments. If your refreshed data differ, use the
counts printed by this report and investigate the sample definition before
interpreting the models.

## 2. Fit the three models

The outcome is the natural logarithm of price per ping. Walk-up apartments
are the reference group, so the high-rise coefficient is the estimated
high-rise difference relative to walk-ups.

```{r}
model_1 <- lm(
  log_price_per_ping ~ building_group,
  data = analysis_data
)

model_2 <- lm(
  log_price_per_ping ~ building_group + DISTRICT,
  data = analysis_data
)

model_3 <- lm(
  log_price_per_ping ~ building_group + DISTRICT + log_area,
  data = analysis_data
)

models <- list(
  "Building type only" = model_1,
  "Add district" = model_2,
  "Add district and floor area" = model_3
)

```

| Model | Formula | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Building type | Pooled high-rise versus walk-up price association. |
| 2 | Building type + district | The association after accounting for district. |
| 3 | Building type + district + log floor area | The association after accounting for district and floor area. |

## 3. Compare the estimated price gaps

Exponentiating a log-price coefficient converts it to a percentage difference.
The intervals below use HC3 robust standard errors.

```{r}
extract_gap <- function(model, model_name) {
  coefficient_name <- "building_groupHigh-rise (11+ floors)"
  if (!coefficient_name %in% names(coef(model))) {
    stop(
      "High-rise coefficient missing in ", model_name,
      ". Check that both building types are present."
    )
  }

  robust_vcov <- sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC3")
  estimate <- coef(model)[coefficient_name]
  standard_error <- sqrt(robust_vcov[coefficient_name, coefficient_name])
  critical_value <- qt(0.975, df = df.residual(model))

  data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    N = nobs(model),
    Gap = 100 * (exp(estimate) - 1),
    Lower = 100 * (exp(estimate - critical_value * standard_error) - 1),
    Upper = 100 * (exp(estimate + critical_value * standard_error) - 1),
    R_squared = summary(model)$r.squared,
    RMSE_log_price = sqrt(mean(residuals(model)^2)),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  Map(extract_gap, models, names(models))
)

knitr::kable(
  transform(
    results,
    Gap = round(Gap, 1),
    Lower = round(Lower, 1),
    Upper = round(Upper, 1),
    R_squared = round(R_squared, 3),
    RMSE_log_price = round(RMSE_log_price, 3)
  ),
  col.names = c(
    "Model", "Transactions", "Gap (%)", "95% CI lower (%)",
    "95% CI upper (%)", "R-squared", "Residual RMSE"
  ),
  caption = "Estimated high-rise price-per-ping difference relative to walk-ups"
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(results, aes(x = Gap, y = reorder(Model, Gap))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey65", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper), height = 0.16,
                 color = "#315B7D", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "#C45A36", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "High-rise price-per-ping gap across model specifications",
    x = "Estimated difference from walk-up apartments (%)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Points show estimates. Bars show 95% HC3 robust confidence intervals."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

**Interpret the output.** Compare how the estimate changes as district and
floor area enter the model. A smaller estimate after adjustment means the
adjusted association differs from the pooled association. It does not, by
itself, identify a causal effect or prove that any one district caused the
change.

## 4. Model fit and residual check

R-squared and residual RMSE describe fit on these same transactions. They do
not measure prediction accuracy on new sales. The residual plot checks for a
visible pattern against floor area that the linear log-area term may miss.

```{r}
fit_summary <- data.frame(
  Model = names(models),
  N = vapply(models, nobs, numeric(1)),
  R_squared = vapply(models, function(model) summary(model)$r.squared, numeric(1)),
  RMSE_log_price = vapply(
    models,
    function(model) sqrt(mean(residuals(model)^2)),
    numeric(1)
  )
)
knitr::kable(transform(
  fit_summary,
  R_squared = round(R_squared, 3),
  RMSE_log_price = round(RMSE_log_price, 3)
))
```

```{r}
diagnostic_data <- data.frame(
  Fitted = fitted(model_3),
  Residual = residuals(model_3),
  Floor_area = analysis_data$FAREA
)

ggplot(diagnostic_data, aes(x = Floor_area, y = Residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, color = "#315B7D") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              color = "#C45A36", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Model 3 residuals by floor area",
    x = "Floor area (ping)",
    y = "Residual in log price per ping"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

Look for a systematic curve or widening spread. Individual residuals can be
large even when the average price gap is estimated with a clear confidence
interval. If a strong pattern appears, discuss a specific adjustment with the
group and compare it using the same sample.

## 5. Limitations and next step

- The estimates describe recorded 2026 transactions in this dataset.
- The earlier years in the snapshot have uneven coverage, so the core analysis
  uses 2026 only.
- Building type and elevator status overlap in this sample, so this analysis
  does not isolate a separate elevator premium.
- Building completion dates are unavailable for the current 2026 sample, so
  building age is not included.
- District-specific gaps are an optional extension. Check the district counts
  first and report uncertainty for any district comparison.

## Suggested presentation takeaway

Use the three estimates from the results table to state how the estimated gap
changes from the pooled model to the district-adjusted model and then to the
model that also adjusts for floor area. Insert the values generated by this
report after the team reproduces and checks them in R.
